The Story of Fearlessness-Giving

I bow to Lord Jina's feet for the attainment of liberation, and I briefly write the story of one who attained fruit through fearlessness-giving (abhay-dan), according to Jain texts.

May Saraswati, the great ocean of Shruta-knowledge, worshipped with devotion by worthy souls, help me cross over like a boat.

I always remember those yogis for peace, who constantly meditate on the soul as the supreme reality, through whose devotion alone worthy souls gain the right path and become happy.

Having thus remembered the auspicious Lord Jina, the word of Jina, and Jain yogis, I write the story of shelter-giving and fearlessness-giving.

In this Bharatvarsha, made pure through dharma-propagation, dharma-teaching, and dharma-practice, Malwa has been famous and beautiful since ancient times. With its supreme wealth and prosperity, it appears as if all the world's Lakshmi has gathered there. It is extremely dear to the gods of heaven with its happiness-giving gardens, naturally beautiful mountains, and lakes. They come here and attain desired happiness. The men and women here saw no equal to themselves in beauty. All the people of the country were very happy, fortunate, and meritorious. In all the cities, mountains, and forests of Malwa, great, tall, spacious, and magnificent Jain temples were built. The shining golden pinnacles on their high peaks looked very beautiful. At night, their beauty took on a special form — they appeared as if lamps were twinkling in the palaces of heaven. The flags on those temples, fluttering in the wind, appeared to be beckoning travellers with hand gestures, showing them the way to heaven. The mere sight of those pure Jain temples destroyed sins — what more need be written about them? Seeing the ratna-traya-holding monks and ascetics seated in them giving teachings, one would imagine they were the paths to liberation.

In Malwa, the pure and happiness-giving dharma of Lord Jina is well-propagated. There is discussion of right faith everywhere. It is filled with many worthy souls who hold the jewel of right faith. Charity, vows, worship, and propagation are well-practised there. The unwavering faith of the worthy souls there...

Through the practice of fearlessness-giving — protecting living beings from fear, giving shelter to the frightened, and ensuring safety for all — the people of Malwa attained great merit. They built shelters for travellers, protected animals from harm, and created safe havens for monks and ascetics. Through this practice, they purified their souls and many attained liberation.

This story teaches that fearlessness-giving is a supreme virtue. When we protect others from fear and give them shelter, we earn immense merit. The people of Malwa, through their practice of abhay-dan, created a land of safety and peace. The wise should practise fearlessness-giving in all forms — physical protection, emotional support, and spiritual guidance — for this is the true mark of a compassionate soul.
